name: Charles University
summary: Prague university where each faculty admits its own: English bachelor's in social sciences, CS, psychology and sport; medicine in three cities.

ib.text: Charles accepts an IB Diploma automatically, with no assessment fee. Each faculty runs its own selection; a few faculty pages still list a recognition fee for foreign diplomas, so ask.

apply.via: Charles's online application (SIS), one per programme

dates.label: Faculty of Social Sciences: applications for 2027/28 open
Second Faculty of Medicine: applications open
Faculty of Social Sciences: early-bird deadline (regular deadline 30 April 2027)
Second Faculty of Medicine: entrance exam in Prague (regular date)
Second Faculty of Medicine: entrance exam in London
Second Faculty of Medicine: entrance exam in Berlin
Second Faculty of Medicine: entrance exam in Prague (alternative date)

programmes.name: Computer Science
programmes.about: Applied and theoretical computer science on a strong maths base: a common first year, then General Computer Science, Databases and Web, or Artificial Intelligence.
programmes.overview: The first year covers mathematical analysis, linear algebra, discrete mathematics, algorithms, data structures, programming, and computer systems such as networking and Linux. The second year adds graph theory, logic, probability and statistics, automata and grammars, database systems and an individual software project, and the third is given to electives and the thesis. Lectures are paired with recitations, and the emphasis is on the core principles of how systems work. Three tracks are available: general computer science, databases and web, and artificial intelligence. Graduates can start work or go on to a master's.
programmes.ib: Grade 6 in Maths AA HL or AI HL; your IB total does not count. IB English at grade 6 proves your English. No entrance exam.
programmes.selectionNote: No exam or ranking test: meet the maths bar (IB Maths HL 6, or the SAT, AP or A-level routes) and prove your English. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

programmes.name: Economics and Finance
programmes.about: Theoretical and applied economics and finance with serious maths and statistics, taught partly by central-bank and banking professionals; electives in finance, economic policy, trade and European integration.
programmes.overview: You learn microeconomics, macroeconomics, mathematical economics, mathematical statistics and finance, with game theory, political economy and the history of economic thought alongside. Teachers include academics as well as professionals from the central bank, commercial banks and business analysis. Electives let you lean toward finance and banking, economic policy, strategic management, international trade or European economic integration. Graduates go into banking, consulting, investment funds and public administration, and many continue to master's programmes in economics, corporate finance or data analysis.
programmes.ib: No entrance exam. Your IB Maths result (AA or AI, SL or HL) earns up to 45 of 100 points and your English up to 45.
programmes.selectionNote: Ranked out of 100: maths 45, English 45, CV and motivation letter 10; the dean sets the cut-off. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.
programmes.closesNote: An early-bird round closes in February

programmes.name: History and Area Studies
programmes.about: Modern history, culture and politics of Central Europe, taught in English alongside Czech-language courses that take you to B2 Czech by graduation.
programmes.overview: The degree studies the history, culture, politics and economics of contemporary Central Europe through compulsory overview courses and electives that let you go deeper into topics that interest you. Czech language training runs through all three years, from basic grammar up to upper-intermediate level, so that later you can discuss specialised topics in Czech. There are no formal tracks. Graduates are prepared for work in the civil service, diplomacy, NGOs, think-tanks, international institutions, private companies and the media, or for a master's at the university in English or Czech.
programmes.ib: No entrance exam: ranked on your record, a motivation letter, a recommendation letter and activities. No Czech needed to apply; it is taught from scratch.
programmes.selectionNote: Scored out of 100: academic record 40, motivation and recommendation letters 40, extracurricular activities 20. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.
programmes.closesNote: An early-bird round closes in February

programmes.name: Politics, Philosophy and Economics
programmes.about: Modelled on Oxford's PPE: three semesters of core courses, then a Politics & Philosophy, Economics & Politics or Philosophy & Economics track.
programmes.overview: The programme links the foundations of domestic and international politics, economics and philosophy, and trains you to analyse social, political and economic problems from complementary angles, including the ethics of political decisions in diverse and unequal societies. After compulsory courses in the first three semesters you choose one of three tracks: politics and philosophy, economics and politics, or philosophy and economics, which sets your electives and thesis focus. Graduates go into politics, diplomacy, public service, policy analysis, journalism, NGOs, banking and business, or on to master's study.
programmes.ib: No entrance exam: ranked on your academic record (65 points) and motivation and activities (35). Strong school maths matters for the economics tracks.
programmes.selectionNote: Applicants within 5 points of the cut-off have an online interview worth up to 6 points either way. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.
programmes.closesNote: An early-bird round closes in February

programmes.name: Social Sciences
programmes.about: Interdisciplinary social science built on research methods, drawing on sociology, public policy, media studies, political science, anthropology, economics and environmental studies.
programmes.overview: This interdisciplinary degree draws on sociology, public policy, media studies, political science, social anthropology, economics and environmental studies, and takes up current questions such as governance, the social effect of media and how society and technology interact. You learn both analytical and interpretative research methods, with attention to research ethics, and prepare a substantial bachelor's thesis. A wide choice of electives lets you build your own profile. Graduates go on to social science master's programmes, research, media, communications, government, NGOs or private companies.
programmes.ib: Two rounds: your record and motivation letter shortlist you, then you write a supervised online essay (350–500 words) on a social issue.
programmes.selectionNote: Round 1: record 30 and letter 20 points; round 2: the essay, 50 of 100. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.
programmes.closesNote: An early-bird round closes in February

programmes.name: Sustainability in Marketing and Media Communication
programmes.about: Communication, media studies and marketing combined with sustainable development: you create media content and learn to judge the environmental impact of campaigns.
programmes.overview: The degree joins communication and media studies and marketing with ideas from sustainable development. You learn to present sustainability topics through media, understand intercultural communication, analyse media messages on social platforms, including the environmental footprint of campaigns, and produce content with photography, text, data visualisation and video. Teaching is project-based and taught on campus in English. Graduates work in press and communications departments or as media analysts for government bodies, companies, NGOs, media agencies and broadcasters, or continue to a related master's.
programmes.ib: No entrance exam: ranked on a motivation letter, CV, a portfolio (or an essay) and a written reflection on a media-and-sustainability example.
programmes.selectionNote: Scored out of 100: motivation letter 30, CV 10, portfolio 30, media reflection 30. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.
programmes.closesNote: An early-bird round closes in February

programmes.name: Liberal Arts and Humanities
programmes.about: An open curriculum centred on philosophy, history and cultural and social anthropology, with few compulsory courses, so you build your own path through the humanities.
programmes.overview: A wide-open curriculum with few compulsory courses centres on philosophy, history, and cultural and social anthropology, with further choices in sociology, psychology, gender studies and art, and a focus on European philosophy, Central European history and the theories and methods of the social sciences. Seminar groups in English build communication skills in a multicultural setting, and you gradually focus on fields of your choice through electives. Graduates work as copywriters, event managers, journalists, media analysts, nonprofit workers and public opinion analysts, or continue to postgraduate study in the humanities and social sciences.
programmes.ib: Admission rests on the online Scio GAP reasoning test; the faculty pays for one sitting. The IB counts as proof of schooling with no assessment.
programmes.selectionNote: You need the percentile the dean sets on the Scio General Academic Prerequisites test, sat online between January and April. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

programmes.name: Psychology
programmes.about: Scientific psychology built on the European EuroPsy standard: cognitive, developmental, social and personality psychology, plus clinical, educational and organisational applications.
programmes.overview: The programme starts with neurophysiology and cognitive, developmental, social and personality psychology, then moves to applied areas such as clinical and health, educational, organizational and forensic psychology, with research methodology, statistics and academic writing alongside. Teaching combines lectures, laboratory-based courses, field excursions and internships in real settings, with links to faculty hospitals, clinical centres and the Czech Academy of Sciences. Electives let you develop your own focus. Graduates continue to a psychology master's, a step toward the European Diploma in Psychology, or work in HR, education, public administration, NGOs and market research.
programmes.ib: No tests or interviews: a portfolio of your grades, motivation letter and CV. English at B2 is shown after admission; an English-taught diploma counts.
programmes.selectionNote: Scored out of 100: penultimate-year grade average 40, motivation letter (max. 650 words) 30, CV and activities 30. Decisions in mid-February.

programmes.name: Science
programmes.about: Biology, chemistry and physics studied side by side for two years with maths and programming, then a third year specialising in one of the three.
programmes.overview: The programme follows a 2+1 plan: everyone takes the same curriculum for two years and then spends the third year on one of three specialisations, biology, chemistry or physics. About a third of the early courses cover mathematics, computer science, programming and professional skills, and the rest is divided evenly between biology, chemistry and physics. Teaching combines lectures with laboratory work in the biological and chemical departments of the science faculty and the physics departments of the mathematics and physics faculty. Graduates move on to related master's programmes or into research, consulting and sustainability-related work.
programmes.ib: Online interview in biology, chemistry and physics plus CV, motivation letter and science grades. Your school sends IB results through IBIS; no paper copies.
programmes.selectionNote: Scored out of 100: online interview 55, motivation letter 25, CV 10, science and maths grades 10. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

programmes.name: Protestant Theology
programmes.about: Biblical studies in the original Hebrew and Greek, Christian traditions, world religions, philosophy and ethics, taught in small groups in central Prague.
programmes.overview: You study biblical studies, with New Testament Greek and ancient Hebrew to read key texts in the original languages, along with the history of European Christianity, church history, dogmatics and systematic theology, theological ethics, philosophy, world religions, practical theology and ecumenical questions. The faculty teaches in small, discussion-based groups in central Prague, with a major theological library at hand, and offers international projects such as partner visits abroad and archaeological excavations. Graduates move on to academic research and further study, or work in religious service, education, culture and social work.
programmes.ib: An oral exam: discuss your motivation and two books you choose from the reading list; 45 of 70 points admits you.
programmes.selectionNote: One oral round with a faculty committee, in late June. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

programmes.name: English Language for Teacher Education
programmes.about: Linguistics, literature in English and language practice for future English teachers, studied as a major with Music Education or Playing Instrument as your second subject.
programmes.overview: This is a two-subject degree, studied together with music education, choral singing or an instrument. The English half centres on linguistics, with attention to both its theory and its practical use, and on the analysis of literature across genres, with language practice aimed at advanced proficiency. You write a bachelor's thesis in English. Graduates can continue to a master's in teaching for secondary schools, or work in state and international institutions.
programmes.ib: Written English test (grammar, vocabulary, reading) set at B2; a C1 certificate can exempt you. Your second subject has its own exam.
programmes.selectionNote: Two exams worth 40 points each: English, and a music talent test or instrument performance for your second subject. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

family.name: Teacher Education in English and Music
family.differs: English major, combined with Music Education or Playing Instrument; written English test.

programmes.name: Music Education for Teacher Education
programmes.about: Music pedagogy in theory and practice for future music teachers, combined with English, Choral Singing or Playing Instrument as your second subject.
programmes.overview: Studied alongside English, choral singing or an instrument, this degree builds music theory, harmony, counterpoint, organology and music history together with practical work: vocal and instrumental preparation, ear training and choral conducting. Pedagogy, psychology and teaching methodology run alongside, with observation and assistant practice in schools. The degree is a stepping stone toward a master's in music education. Graduates can work as teaching assistants or pedagogues in school and out-of-school music settings, or in cultural administration.
programmes.ib: Talent exam in singing, musicality and piano or violin, each with a pass mark. Your second subject has its own exam.
programmes.selectionNote: Two exams worth 40 points each; missing the pass mark in any part of the talent exam scores it zero. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

family.name: Teacher Education in English and Music
family.differs: Music Education major, combined with English, Choral Singing or Playing Instrument; talent exam.

programmes.name: Choral Singing for Teacher Education
programmes.about: Conducting technique, reading vocal scores, choir voice training, aural analysis and choral literature, studied as a major with Music Education.
programmes.overview: This choral specialisation is studied with music education. You learn conducting technique, playing from vocal scores, vocal training within a choir, aural analysis and choral literature for different kinds of ensemble, alongside music theory, harmony, history and school-based teaching practice. Performing and demonstrating music yourself is central. Graduates can work in schools, cultural centres and churches, though independent conducting work calls for further study, and the degree leads on to a master's in music education.
programmes.ib: Practical exam in choral singing and conducting skills, plus the Music Education talent exam.
programmes.selectionNote: Two exams worth 40 points each, one per subject. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

family.name: Teacher Education in English and Music
family.differs: Choral Singing major, combined with Music Education; conducting and choir training.

programmes.name: Playing Instrument for Teacher Education
programmes.about: Piano or violin for musicians aiming to teach rather than perform: individual lessons, chamber music, improvisation and orchestra, with English or Music Education as second subject.
programmes.overview: Studied alongside English, this degree is aimed at musicians who want an education career rather than a performing one. You choose piano or violin as your main instrument and study solo performance, chamber music, improvisation and ensemble playing, together with the construction of instruments and the history of instrumental literature. Graduates can teach in music schools, assist with cultural activities for children, or work in museums and cultural organisations; teaching in primary or secondary schools requires a master's.
programmes.ib: Perform a memorised piano or violin programme: etudes plus Baroque, Classical, Romantic and 20th-century pieces. Your second subject has its own exam.
programmes.selectionNote: Two exams worth 40 points each, one per subject. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

family.name: Teacher Education in English and Music
family.differs: Piano or violin major, combined with English or Music Education; performance exam.

programmes.name: Coach
programmes.about: Sports coaching grounded in sport science, pedagogy and psychology, specialising in one sport: athletics, gymnastics, swimming, football, ice hockey, volleyball, basketball, tennis, handball or combat sports.
programmes.overview: You study pedagogy, psychology, biomedicine, sports training and teaching methods relevant to a chosen sport. The first one to two years establish applied sport science and basic athletic skills, which you then apply in specialised courses and practical training in years two and three. You choose one of ten sports: track and field, gymnastics, swimming, football, ice hockey, volleyball, basketball, tennis, handball or combat sports. Graduates are able to design and carry out training programmes for athletes of all ages and performance levels.
programmes.ib: Online interview in English on your motivation letter and a short text; send a CV, recommendation, English certificate and sports doctor's note.
programmes.selectionNote: Scored 0–30: motivation letter, spoken English and discussion of an English text, 10 each; 15 needed. A later second round also ran in 2026. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

family.name: Coaching
family.differs: Coaching in one chosen sport, from athletics and swimming to ice hockey and combat sports.
family.cardLine: Coaching in one sport you choose

programmes.name: Fitness Coach
programmes.about: Designing exercise programmes for different groups: exercise physiology, biomechanics, nutrition and training theory, applied in strength training, athletics and gymnastics.
programmes.overview: The theory side covers pedagogy and psychology, physiology and adaptation, biomechanics, sports training and nutrition, together with general didactic principles. It is applied in practice-oriented courses in strength training, athletics, gymnastics and other sports. The first year and part of the second build basic motor skills and the principles of applied sport science, and later years combine specialised didactics with practical training. Graduates can design and run fitness and exercise programmes with varied goals for different groups of people.
programmes.ib: Online interview in English on your motivation letter and a short text; send a CV, recommendation, English certificate and sports doctor's note.
programmes.selectionNote: Scored 0–30: motivation letter, spoken English and discussion of an English text, 10 each; 15 needed. A later second round also ran in 2026. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

family.name: Coaching
family.differs: Fitness and exercise programmes for the general public and athletes, with nutrition and strength training.
family.cardLine: Exercise programmes, nutrition and strength training

programmes.name: Physiotherapy
programmes.about: Diagnosis and movement therapy for disorders of the musculoskeletal system, qualifying you as a physiotherapist to WCPT standards, with practice in hospitals, rehabilitation and sport.
programmes.overview: You are trained to work as a physiotherapist in prevention, diagnosis, treatment and rehabilitation, using a broad range of physiotherapeutic methods including treatments based on physical agents, and learning to judge whether a treatment works. Teaching mixes theory with practical skills on modern equipment, led by staff who are often practising healthcare professionals and researchers. The programme follows international physiotherapy standards. Graduates work in hospitals, rehabilitation centres, social care facilities, spas and sports facilities.
programmes.ib: Online interview in English on your motivation letter, spoken English and a physiotherapy text; send a CV, recommendation and English certificate.
programmes.selectionNote: Scored 0–25: motivation letter 5, spoken English 10, understanding a professional text 10. A later second round also ran in 2026. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

programmes.name: General Medicine (First Faculty of Medicine)
programmes.about: Six-year MUDr. degree at the First Faculty in central Prague; entry is a science test followed by online multiple mini-interviews.
programmes.overview: This six-year degree, taught in English, gives a firm footing in both theoretical and clinical medicine and leads to the MUDr. title. Graduates go on as practising doctors, and many are offered jobs before their final year ends. The qualification allows you to work or train further as a specialist elsewhere in Europe and in North America, and graduates may also go into medical research or postgraduate specialist programmes.
programmes.ib: Test in biology, chemistry and physics, then five online mini-interviews. IB 36+ with HL Biology, HL Chemistry and a third science or maths HL, each 6+, adds a 10% bonus.
programmes.selectionNote: The test (with any bonus, final IB results only) decides who reaches the interviews; places go on interview score alone. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

family.name: General Medicine
family.differs: Test plus online mini-interviews; IB bonus points, no waiver; fee in euros.

programmes.name: General Medicine (Second Faculty of Medicine)
programmes.about: Six-year MD in English since 1992, taught at the Plzeňská campus and the Motol and Homolka university hospitals; accredited by the Medical Board of California.
programmes.overview: The first three years build a common base in anatomy, cell biology, pathology, pathophysiology, immunology and biostatistics, with bioethics, psychology and nursing courses for patient communication, and contact with patients from the start. Years four to six move into hospital block rotations at the Motol and Homolka hospitals, where you manage real cases in clinical teams, with simulation and optional internships in Czech or foreign hospitals. The degree ends with state exams in public health, internal medicine, surgery, gynaecology and obstetrics, and paediatrics, and leads to residency, research or healthcare leadership.
programmes.ib: Written test (biology, chemistry, physics, logic) and interview. IB waiver: 35+ points with 19 from HL Biology, HL Chemistry and Maths or Physics; predicted grades count.
programmes.selectionNote: Up to 25 waivers go to the best IB, EB and BS applicants; ask for one with your application. Otherwise sit the test in Prague (3 June or 22 July) or abroad.
programmes.closesNote: Exam registration and waiver requests too

family.name: General Medicine
family.differs: Test and interview, or an IB waiver at 35 points; 2027 dates are out: apply by 30 April 2027.

programmes.name: General Medicine (Third Faculty of Medicine)
programmes.about: Six-year MUDr. degree taught through an integrated curriculum: theory and preclinical subjects are linked, and common clinical problems are taught through problem-based learning.
programmes.overview: This six-year degree gives a complete medical education with extra emphasis on preventive health care, and it is taught in English alongside a Czech-language track that has run since the early 1990s. Clinical training is central, which is why international students are expected to learn enough Czech by the second year to talk with patients and hospital staff. Graduates receive the MUDr. title, which permits practice in all medical disciplines and is recognised internationally, and the faculty is accredited for American students.
programmes.ib: Tests in biology and chemistry, then an interview. Up to 25 enter without the exam: HL Chemistry, HL Biology and HL English summing to 19 or more.
programmes.selectionNote: Send the waiver form with your application. Main exam in Prague in late May, or at agency sittings abroad. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

family.name: General Medicine
family.differs: Biology and chemistry tests plus interview, or a waiver with HL Chemistry, Biology and English at 19; 90 places.

programmes.name: General Medicine (Plzeň)
programmes.about: Six-year MUDr. degree in Plzeň: two theoretical years, two preclinical years with bedside teaching from year three, then two clinical years.
programmes.overview: The first two years cover anatomy, histology, embryology, biophysics, biochemistry and physiology, years three and four add pathology, microbiology, immunology and pharmacology, and the last two years are entirely clinical. Bedside teaching begins in the first year, and each year is split into winter and summer semesters with exam periods. Teaching is entirely in English at the medical faculty in Pilsen. Graduates receive the MUDr. degree, awarded in a ceremony at the Carolinum in Prague, and can practise medicine internationally.
programmes.ib: Written test in biology, chemistry and physics (75 questions), in Plzeň or at agency sittings abroad. No IB waiver; the IB needs no assessment fee.
programmes.selectionNote: The dean sets the pass mark from the number of places; one attempt per year. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

family.name: General Medicine
family.differs: Written test in biology, chemistry and physics, no interview; CZK 390,000 a year.

programmes.name: General Medicine (Hradec Králové)
programmes.about: Six-year MUDr. degree with clinical teaching in groups of five to seven at the university hospital, an adaptation programme before you start, and compulsory Czech classes in years 1–2.
programmes.overview: The first two years teach the structure and function of the human body from molecules to organ systems, with first-aid training and simulation-centre work. Years three and four add preclinical subjects and propaedeutics of internal medicine and surgery, taught in the university hospital, and the final two years are fully clinical in internal medicine, surgery, gynaecology and obstetrics, paediatrics and preventive medicine. Teaching uses virtual dissection tables, 3D scans and microscopes, clinical groups of five to seven students, and hospital placements in years two and four, including abroad. Graduates can work as general practitioners or specialists, or pursue doctoral study.
programmes.ib: Test in biology, chemistry and physics or maths (60 points) plus an interview (40). Sit it with partner agencies abroad or online through Scio.
programmes.selectionNote: The top 105 applicants, ties included, are admitted. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

family.name: General Medicine
family.differs: Test (maths can replace physics) and interview; online sitting via Scio; 105 places.

programmes.name: Dentistry (First Faculty of Medicine)
programmes.about: Five-year MDDr. degree in dentistry, including its theoretical fields, at the First Faculty in Prague; entry is a science test followed by online multiple mini-interviews.
programmes.overview: This five-year degree in English is built on both theoretical and practical dentistry and leads to the MDDr. title. Graduates are trained to work as dentists in practice and in theory, and most are offered jobs during their final year. They can go on to postgraduate specialist dental study or into research, and the faculty's language and preparatory institute helps international students settle into study in a new cultural setting.
programmes.ib: Test in biology, chemistry and physics, then five online mini-interviews. IB 36+ with HL Biology, HL Chemistry and a third science or maths HL, each 6+, adds a 10% bonus.
programmes.selectionNote: The test decides who reaches the interviews; places go on interview score. 30 places in 2026/27. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

family.name: Dentistry
family.differs: Test plus online mini-interviews, IB bonus points; 30 places; fee in euros.

programmes.name: Dentistry (Plzeň)
programmes.about: Five-year MDDr. degree in Plzeň; years three to five are devoted to clinical dentistry, preparing you for general practice or specialisation.
programmes.overview: The first two years concentrate on theoretical disciplines such as anatomy, histology, biochemistry and physiology together with pre-clinical dentistry, and years three to five are entirely clinical practice in stomatology, covering diagnosis and treatment. Bedside teaching begins in the first year, and each year is split into winter and summer semesters with exam periods. Teaching is in English at the faculty in Pilsen. Graduates receive the MDDr. degree at a ceremony in Prague, and the qualification is widely recognised internationally.
programmes.ib: Written test in biology, chemistry and physics (75 questions), in Plzeň or at agency sittings abroad. No IB waiver; the IB needs no assessment fee.
programmes.selectionNote: The dean sets the pass mark from the number of places; one attempt per year. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

family.name: Dentistry
family.differs: Written test in biology, chemistry and physics, no interview; CZK 390,000 a year.

programmes.name: Dentistry (Hradec Králové)
programmes.about: Five-year MDDr. degree with two students per chair in clinical lessons and training in digital methods such as intraoral scanning, CAD/CAM and 3D printing.
programmes.overview: Theoretical, preclinical and clinical subjects run together from the start: you work in a phantom laboratory in the first semester and see patients by the third year. Teaching is hands-on with very small groups, two students per chair in clinical lessons, and uses digital scanning, CAD/CAM and 3D printing. Graduates receive the MDDr. degree and can carry out the full range of dental work without supervision; unlike doctors, dentists need no further mandatory training, though specialisation is available.
programmes.ib: Test in biology, chemistry and physics or maths (60 points) plus an interview (40). Sit it with partner agencies abroad or online through Scio.
programmes.selectionNote: The top 25 applicants, ties included, are admitted. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

family.name: Dentistry
family.differs: Test (maths can replace physics) and interview; 25 places; digital dentistry.

programmes.name: Pharmacy
programmes.about: Five-year pharmacy degree that meets the EU directive for pharmacists, with elective subjects letting you specialise; taught at the Faculty of Pharmacy in Hradec Králové.
programmes.overview: This five-year master's degree follows European standards, and alongside the compulsory subjects you can specialise by choosing recommended and optional courses that fit your interests. Graduates are qualified for the full range of pharmaceutical work: manufacturing and testing medicines, wholesale distribution, community pharmacy, hospital pharmacy and advising patients. The degree also forms a base for postgraduate and doctoral study.
programmes.ib: Test in chemistry, biology, botany and English grammar. IB waiver: 32+ points with Biology (HL 5 or SL 6) and Chemistry, Maths or Physics (HL 5 or SL 6).
programmes.selectionNote: Sit the test online through Scio or in person; the dean sets the pass mark. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

notes: Each faculty runs its own admission, fee and timetable, and each programme is a separate online application with its own fee; Charles has no rolling admission and grants no individual extensions.
For medicine the faculty matters: fees run from CZK 390,000 a year in Plzeň to €24,250 at the First Faculty, and IB-based exam waivers exist at the Second and Third Faculties and in Pharmacy.
Charles publishes each programme's conditions at least four months before its deadline; until a faculty posts its 2027 rules, these pages show the 2026 ones.
